questions.q: Write the equilibrium constant expression ($K_c$) for the following heterogeneous reaction:\n$$\text{CaCO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$$
questions.explain: The concentrations of pure solids and pure liquids are constant and are omitted from the equilibrium expression. Thus, $K_c = [\text{CO}_2]$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: For the reaction $2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$, what is the relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$?
questions.explain: The relationship is $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$. Here, $\Delta n_g = (\text{moles product gas}) - (\text{moles reactant gas}) = 2 - (2+1) = -1$. Therefore, $K_p = K_c(RT)^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: If the equilibrium constant for $A \rightleftharpoons B$ is $K_1 = 2$, what is the equilibrium constant for the reaction $2B \rightleftharpoons 2A$?
questions.explain: Reversing the reaction inverts $K​$ ($1/K_1 = 1/2$). Multiplying coefficients by 2 raises the new constant to the power of 2. New $K = (1/2)^2 = 1/4 = 0.25$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Calculate $K_c$ for the reaction $2\text{NO}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$ given the equilibrium concentrations: $[\text{NO}] = 0.2\,\text{M}$, $[\text{N}_2] = 0.1\,\text{M}$, and $[\text{O}_2] = 0.1\,\text{M}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which statement about the value of the equilibrium constant $K​$ is true?
options: A large $K​$ ($K \gg 1$) indicates that reactants are favored at equilibrium.
A small $K​$ ($K \ll 1$) indicates that products are favored at equilibrium.
The value of $K​$ is independent of temperature.
A large $K​$ ($K \gg 1$) indicates that products are favored at equilibrium.
questions.explain: If $K​$ is very large, the numerator (products) is much larger than the denominator (reactants), meaning the equilibrium favors the products.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: For the reaction $\text{H}_2(g) + \text{I}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}(g)$, $K_c = 50$ at a certain temperature. If the volume of the container is halved, what happens to the value of $K_c$?
options: It increases by a factor of 4.
questions.explain: The equilibrium constant $K_c$ is dependent only on temperature. Changing volume or pressure shifts the equilibrium position but does not change the constant $K_c$ itself.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Determine the units of $K_c$ for the reaction: $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)$ (where concentration is in mol L$^{-1}$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: At 298 K, if $K_c = 1.0 \times 10^{10}$ for a reaction, what can be said about the standard Gibbs free energy change $\Delta G^\circ$?
questions.explain: $\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K$. If $K​$ is very large (positive), $\ln K$ is positive, making $\Delta G^\circ$ a large negative value, indicating a spontaneous forward reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Given the reaction $A(g) \rightleftharpoons 2B(g)$. At equilibrium, the partial pressure of $A​$ is 0.5 atm and $B​$ is 2.0 atm. Calculate $K_p$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: When writing the equilibrium expression for a reaction in aqueous solution involving water as a solvent (e.g., hydrolysis), the concentration of water is:
options: Omitted or incorporated into the constant value.
questions.explain: In dilute aqueous solutions, the concentration of water is effectively constant and is conventionally omitted from the equilibrium expression or incorporated into the constant (e.g., $K_w$, $K_a$).
questions.subject: Chemistry
